verifications.claim: Artemis II is a crewed lunar mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Artemis II test flight will be NASA’s first mission with crew aboard the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft. The crew includes Commander Reid Wiseman...'; R2: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS rocket, with the Orion spacecraft atop carrying NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover...'; R3: 'send four astronauts on a journey around the moon'; R7: 'NASA Artemis II mission to send four crew on 10-day mission to do a lunar fly-by'; R8: 'Artemis II is the first crewed mission... send a crew of 4... around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Artemis II is crewed and involves a lunar flyby/orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled for no earlier than April 1, 2026, from Launch Pad 39B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'set to launch no earlier than 6:24 p.m. ET today, Wednesday, April 1, 2026... Launch Pad 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'; R7: 'April 1: NASA Artemis II... from KSC’s Launch Pad 39-B at 6:35 p.m.'
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly uses 'no earlier than April 1, 2026' from Pad 39B; R7 confirms the date and pad.

verifications.claim: Artemis II (NASA SLS/Orion) is scheduled for April 1, 2026 (6:24 PM ET) from Kennedy Space Center Pad 39B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'NASA's Artemis II mission... SLS spacecraft... no earlier than 6:24 p.m. ET... April 1, 2026... Launch Pad 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: R3 matches exactly on date, time, rocket/spacecraft, and pad; actual liftoff was 6:35 p.m. per other sources, but claim specifies scheduled time.

verifications.claim: ViaSat-3 F3 (SpaceX) is scheduled for April 2026 from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Late April: SpaceX ViaSat-3 F3... Location: Pad 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'; R5: 'ViaSat-3 F3... NET April' (Kennedy Space Center); R7: 'TBD, no earlier than late April 2026: SpaceX Falcon Heavy on the ViaSat-3 F3... from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Pad 39-A'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm SpaceX ViaSat-3 F3 in April 2026 (late/NET) from KSC Pad 39A.

verifications.claim: Griffin Mission One (SpaceX Falcon Heavy) is scheduled for July 2026 (TBD) from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Demonstration flight of the Astrobotic Griffin lander... NET H2 2026' (Kennedy Space Center, FH); R7: 'TBD, no earlier than July 2026: SpaceX Falcon Heavy flying Astrobotic’s Griffin lunar lander'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Griffin on Falcon Heavy NET July/H2 2026 from KSC; 'Mission One' aligns with demonstration flight.

verifications.claim: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (SpaceX) is scheduled for September 2026 (TBD) from Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: Only spectators with specialized Artemis II Launch Viewing Packages can enter the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex on the designated launch days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On Artemis II targeted launch dates, only guests with an Artemis II Launch Viewing Package will be allowed entry to the visitor complex. No other form of admission, including annual passes, will be valid.'
verifications.reasoning: R1 states exactly this policy for Artemis II launch dates.

verifications.claim: SpaceX conducts regular Starlink, commercial, and NASA cargo/crew launches from LC-39A (KSC) and SLC-40 (Cape Canaveral).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: Numerous Starlink from SLC-40, crew/cargo/commercial from LC-39A (e.g., 'Crew-12... from SLC-40', 'Starlink... from Space Launch Complex 40'); R4/R5 list SpaceX launches of these types from both pads.
verifications.reasoning: Sources document regular SpaceX Starlink (SLC-40), NASA cargo/crew (LC-39A/SLC-40), commercial from both sites.
